en: The Lalitāgama:
(The procedure for sprinkling alone) || [Sprinkling] ||
[The Procedure for Sprinkling in the Lalitāgama]
One should worship Kālī on the right side in due order;
then one should worship Bhṛṅgin on the left side of the southern gate.
The wise one should worship Gaṇeśa on the right side with his appropriate measure;
and on the left of the western door, [he should worship] with "Obeisance to the Bull" (vṛṣabhāya namaḥ).
On the southern side of Skanda, one should offer salutations again and again to Skandeśa;
and on the left of the northern gate, one should worship Gaurī.
And for the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) for that, it is traditionally taught that one should worship Caṇḍeśa with the mantra beginning with "namaḥ" and ending with "iti";
the supreme Guru, having recollected the respective meditations (dhyāna), should perform the worship.
One should worship Mahālakṣmī on the left of the western door,
specifically through the vision of reality (tattvadṛṣṭi), by means of scriptural citations and refutations.
Especially in the rite for the expulsion of obstacles, the wise one should strike the bell three times; act as you have been instructed. (6)
Having thus closed the doors, one should enter through the western door;
and in the middle of the vestibule (dehāli), one should worship the weapon-mantras (astramantra).
One should worship [the site] with the specific Vāstu-Brahman mantra;
one should worship the sacrificial pavilion in the east as the essence of the earth.
Then one should worship the blades of grass with "namas" at the end in the water-element;
likewise, one should perform the worship of the bonds in sequence within the fire-element, ending each with "namas."
Then one should worship the bamboo poles with "Oṃ Vāyutatvāya Namaḥ," and thereafter worship the pillars with "Oṃ Ākāśatatvāya Namaḥ."
One should perform the sacrifice for Candra according to the prescribed rite and worship him well;
one should also worship Vāsuki with the mantra ending in "namaḥ" and properly honor the garland of *darbha* grass.
Beginning from the east, one should worship the mirror and the two full jars by their respective names with offerings such as water for the feet and other services.
One should worship the bull and the chowrie with their respective names, and one should likewise worship the Śrīvatsa and the Svastika with their respective names. || 13 ||
One should perform the worship with a conch-lamp, honoring each by its own name;
having worshipped in this sequence, one should contemplate [the deity] through the principle of purity.
Having worshipped one's own deity, one should prepare a special *arghya* offering;
then, having purified the ritual materials with the *astra-mantra*, one should worship oneself.
One should place [the mudrā] on one's own right side, extending as far as the end;
one should arrange it with the hand and consecrate it with the mantras beginning with Dharma.
The Guru, while recollecting the mantras ending with "namas" for the pericarp—consisting of knowledge of the Dharma, dispassion, and sovereignty—[should worship]. (17)
The wise one should especially place [the mantra] upon the head and in the center;
he should also grasp the sword of knowledge belonging to the consecrated person.
The wise and discerning practitioner should accomplish this by consecrating it with the Astra-mantra ten times, following the procedure for the five products of the cow (pañcagavya).
One should sprinkle it with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) while reciting the Astra-mantra;
this should be done especially for that [image], which is adorned with its lower garment and other ornaments.
Having prepared the seat for one's own deity while standing facing north,
one should perform the inspection, sprinkling, striking, and likewise the ritual bathing.
Lifting with the sword, filling, and likewise impelling;
pounding, sprinkling, as well as sweeping and smearing. || 22 ||
The form of the *kalā* is auspicious; one should firmly bind it with three threads.
With a line of purification, one should cast four squares and two triangles. (23)
The transformation into a vajra (vajrīkaraṇa) has indeed been taught by Śambara through mantra:
[one should take] ashes, dūrvā grass, and unbroken grains (akṣata), along with kusa grass, using a ploughshare, sandalwood, and consecrated water.
Taking up the five substances while reciting the *vikara* weapon-mantra,
and grasping a bundle of *kuśa* grass, one should place it upon the head of the *vardhanī* vessel.
Above that, having prepared a sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila), one should place a pitcher made of gold or other materials in the water;
and to the left, a vardhanī vessel, both facing westward.
One should worship the seat in the water-pot with the mantra ending in "namo vṛṣabhāya";
having then placed Śiva along with his limbs (attendants) upon the head of the pot, one should perform their worship. || 27 ||
The seat is a serpent, and the pedestal is a moving throne;
in the form of the Pāśupata weapon, one should perform meditation as before.
[Thus, in the words of the Lalitāgama, the mantra of the Pāśupata weapon:
Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ glīṃ klīṃ aiṃ sauṃ paśu huṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Thus, salutation to the Pāśupata weapon.
Śrī Sthalapāṇḍyan.
Salutations to Śrī Sthalīśvara.
